name: Lean BBQ Chicken and Rice Bowls
intro_html: Lean, sweet, smoky, and stupidly cheap. This is the leanest bowl in the rotation at just 4 grams of fat, and it still brings 35 grams of protein for around $1.95 a bowl (at everyday cost). The sugar-free BBQ sauce does the heavy lifting on flavor without wrecking the macros.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 5 cups, drained (840 g)
BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): about 7/8 cup (224 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): about 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
Olive Oil: ~2 tbsp to cook chicken (90 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste / rub (4 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_closing_html: That is about $1.95 a bowl (at everyday cost) versus $11 or more for a fast-casual chicken bowl. Catch chicken on sale at $1.95/lb and that number drops even lower.
shop_smart: Chicken on sale is the whole game. When breast drops to a sale price, buy a big pack and freeze it in two-pound bags. That one trip is a month of these bowls.
Sugar-free sauce, same flavor. The no-sugar BBQ tastes nearly identical to the regular and saves you the sugar and a few carbs per serving.
Fat free cheese stretches the protein. A quarter cup adds 9 grams of protein for 45 calories and zero fat. It is one of the best macro deals in the dairy aisle.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice. Three and a half cups dry jasmine with water per the package, then set aside.
Cube the chicken breast, season it with the salt and black pepper, and cook in a large skillet with the olive oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 165F inside.
Turn the heat to low, pour in the BBQ sauce, and toss until every piece is coated.
Drain the corn and warm it through.
Combine the rice, BBQ chicken, and corn in your big pot and stir. Fold in the shredded cheddar.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total food weight by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container. Every bowl lands near 380 calories and 35 grams of protein at only 4 grams of fat.
upsell_html: High-protein dinners for about $1.95 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: A lean, sweet, smoky meal-prep bowl. Fourteen servings at about 380 calories, 35 grams of protein, and only 4 grams of fat for roughly $1.95 each (at everyday cost).

recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 3.5 lb raw (1587 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 5 cups, drained (840 g)
BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free), about 7/8 cup (224 g)
Fat Free Cheddar, about 1 3/4 cups shredded (196 g)
Olive Oil, ~2 tbsp to cook chicken (90 g)
Black Pepper, to taste / rub (4 g)
steps: Cook 3.5 cups dry jasmine rice per the package and set aside.
Season the cubed chicken with salt and black pepper and cook it in a large skillet with the olive oil until it reaches 165F.
Lower the heat, add the BBQ sauce, and toss to coat.
Combine rice, BBQ chicken, and corn in a large pot and fold in the cheddar.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 equal containers.
